_meta.description: Trigger phrase patterns for .claude/hooks/workflow-trigger.js (#2816). Adding or widening a trigger phrase is a data edit here, matching the policy 02-github-workflow.md already states for trigger-flag-allowlist.json: recognized flags are data, not a hook edit. Patterns moved; meanings did not.
_meta.consumer: .claude/hooks/workflow-trigger.js — compiled once per invocation, before the fast-path check
_meta.compositionDecision: Patterns are data; COMPOSITION IS NOT. reviewTrigger, analysisMatch and testPlanApprovalTrigger are conjunctions of a pattern, a co-requirement and exclusions against sibling triggers, and those relationships stay in code. See Construction/Design-Decisions/2026-09-07-trigger-patterns-composition-stays-in-code.md for the rejected `requires`/`excludes` schema.
_meta.routingNotes: Routing notes (#2999) moved here from the always-on 02-github-workflow rule: the trigger-word table, the review routing table and the Flag Pass-Through Convention. The hook appends a route's notes to its additionalContext only when that route fires, so a session sees each convention in the turn it applies and nowhere else. Optional: absent or malformed, the hook emits its [INVOKE] line unchanged.

workflowTriggerPrefix.description: Trigger prefixes routed to /bug, /enhancement and /proposal. The captured group is the trigger type.

workTrigger.description: Any prompt starting with 'work '. Deliberately broad — the issue number or status filter is extracted opportunistically afterwards.

doneTrigger.description: Standalone 'done' or 'done #N' at message start. Contextual detection (are there active issues) happens later.

reviewAtStart.description: Anchored at the start so assistant output mentioning a review command does not re-trigger routing.

strictIssueRef.description: An EXPLICIT issue reference. Required by triggers that mutate or route to a command, where picking up a stray conversational number would be costly.

looseIssueRef.description: Also accepts a bare two-or-more-digit number. Used ONLY by the analysis trigger, which is read-only, so a false positive costs a STOP reminder rather than an action. Deliberately distinct from strictIssueRef — collapsing the two would change what routes.

approvalVerb.description: Approval verb for the verbal test-plan approval trigger (#2815). Never sufficient alone.

testPlanRef.description: Explicit test-plan reference, hyphenated or spaced, singular or plural.

refreshFlag.description: Cache-refresh flag on the commands help path.

harnessFrame.description: A prompt the harness generated rather than the user typed: a background-task notification, a subagent hand-back, an agent message or a cross-session message (#3163). Anchored at the start of the (trimmed) prompt, so a user who quotes a marker mid-sentence is still a user. UserPromptSubmit input carries no field naming the prompt source, so this text framing is the only signal; it is observed harness behavior, not documented. Used only to exempt such prompts from the analysis trigger. Optional: absent, nothing is exempted and the analysis trigger behaves as before.

triggerWords.text:
**Trigger-word routing.** A message starting with a trigger prefix routes to its command:
`bug:` → `/bug` (bug issue, standard template) · `enhancement:` → `/enhancement` (enhancement issue, standard template) · `proposal:` → `/proposal` (proposal document + tracking issue) · `idea:` → `/proposal` (alias).
Each command creates the issue, reports the number, and STOPs. Do NOT proceed to implementation until the user explicitly says "work".
Flags are extracted from the message and appended to the invocation rather than left in the title, so no `--`-prefixed token becomes part of an issue's identity: `enhancement: add dark mode --prior-art` → `/enhancement add dark mode --prior-art`.

reviewRouting.text:
**Review routing.** `review` with an issue reference (`#N`), at the start of the message (optionally after "please"), routes to `/review-issue` with every `#N` and the flags:
`review #42` → `/review-issue 42` · `review #42 #43 #44` → `/review-issue 42 43 44` · `please review #42` → `/review-issue 42` · `review #42 --with security` → `/review-issue 42 --with security` · `review #42 --mode solo --force` → `/review-issue 42 --mode solo --force`.
`review` is a **tracked action** (routes to a command), not an analysis keyword; `evaluate`, `analyze`, `assess`, `investigate`, `check` and `verify` remain passive analysis triggers that inject a STOP reminder. `review` without an issue number does not route.

flagPassThrough.text:
**Flag pass-through convention** — applies to every routing path; commands gaining flags later inherit it.
- **Extraction is by token shape.** A token is a flag when it is `--` followed by a letter. A bare `--` separator, a `---` rule, and `--` inside prose are not flags and are preserved verbatim in title text.
- **No flag-shaped token is ever discarded.** Unrecognized flags pass through to the command, which reports them through its own error handling. Silent truncation is never correct — a dropped flag gives a narrowed result with nothing to notice.
- **Recognized flags are data,** per command, in `.claude/metadata/trigger-flag-allowlist.json`. Adding a flag is a data edit, not a hook edit.
- **Declaration governs value attachment only.** A recognized flag may claim the following token as its value (`--with security`); an unrecognized one may not, so trailing prose is not swallowed into the argument list.
- **How much a recognized flag claims is declared per flag (#2770).** An entry is a plain flag string (one token, the default) or an object adding `"attach": "rest-of-line"`, claiming every remaining token so a flag can take prose (`/proposal --update`). Per flag, not a mode switch — every other flag keeps the one-token default. `"attach": "none"` (#3314) declares a switch that claims nothing, so `work 383 --nonstop now` carries `--nonstop` alone.
- **A rest-of-line value stops at the next flag-shaped token.** `--update rewrite the intro --assignee octocat` binds `rewrite the intro` and leaves `--assignee` its own value; absorbing a following flag into prose would discard it silently. `--flag=value` carries its own value and never claims following tokens.

workRouting.text:
**Work routing.** A message starting with `work` that names an issue (`work #N`, `work on 123`, `work issue 45`) routes to `/work N` once the hook confirms the issue has a branch assignment — an unassigned issue is refused with the `/assign-branch` remedy. `work all in <status>` routes a batch to `/work --status <status>` only when `<status>` is a status configured in `.gh-pmu.json`.
Flags typed after it are passed through, by the convention below: `work 383 --nonstop --concurrent` → `/work 383 --nonstop --concurrent` · `work all in ready --nonstop` → `/work --status ready --nonstop`.

doneRouting.text: **Done routing.** `done` with issue numbers routes to `/done` with them; a bare `done` routes only when some issue is in review. `/done` moves `in_review` → `done` only — `/work` owns `in_progress` → `in_review`. Issues close only when the user says "Done".
